cases.title: listed modules whose cycle closes only through an import() inside a function are ordered by their load-time imports, and share one instance each
cases.note: a.ts imports b.ts while it loads; b.ts imports a.ts only when later() is called, which puts no constraint on the order. So b registers first, and a's copy takes b from its shim. b's copy resolves its lazy import of a to a's late shim, which reads the registry when a value is read; by the time the step calls later(), a is registered. The step bundle inlines neither module.

folder.wmill.yaml:
defaultTs: bun
includes: ["f/**"]
folder.f/repro/lib/a.ts:
import { b } from './b.ts';
export function a() { return 'a' + b(); }
folder.f/repro/lib/b.ts:
export function b() { return 'b'; }
export async function later() { const { a } = await import('./a.ts'); return a(); }

cases.title: a function-level import() whose function runs while its module loads, before the imported module registers, fails with the not-registered error naming its key, and works once the module is registered
cases.note: b.ts calls later() at top level and keeps the error. The import() inside it is not an ordering edge, so b still registers before a, and the read of a through a's late shim fails, naming a's contract key. The step's later call reads a after its registration and gets it, never an undefined export.
